slides.texte_overlay:
quiet detachment habits that
protect your peace

not taking the bait

when someone tries to start drama, answer calmly or not at all. refusing to take the bait is the quietest way to show that your peace isn't up for negotiation.

letting silence answer

you don't have to reply to every unkind comment. silence is often the most powerful response, and it saves you hours of rewriting angry messages in your head.

feeding your mind better

i stopped feeding my mind gossip and endless scrolling and started feeding it something calm and interesting. drama slowly lost its grip on my attention.
slides.texte_sophia:
feeding your mind better

i swapped gossip and scrolling for 5 minutes a day on one lesson in the Sophia app, a myth or a planet. my mind got calmer, and drama simply stopped interesting me.

slides.texte_overlay:
caring about effort

focus on doing your part well instead of controlling how people react. their opinions are theirs to manage, and your peace depends on letting that go.

releasing old versions

stop defending who you were five years ago. letting old mistakes and old opinions go makes room for the calmer, wiser person you're slowly and quietly becoming.
